And that game was more feature-complete and polished than this game; all while having personality and being stylish. This game lacks charm, the UI is utterly boring and feels outdated. The rhythm game ditches the Garupa feel and caters to the Sekai style which is disappointing. If it weren't for the songs and the bands, I would've dropped the game already. Every time I play this game I see a new bug, every time there's a new feature it's got formatting issues or just buggy as heck. It's like nobody tested this game and it's frustrating. I want this game to improve and become an actual good game, but the fact that it even released in this sorry state has already soured my opinion on it heavily. -— Rant incoming!!! Something that really really disappointed me about this game is that it did not need to exist. I was waiting 3 years for Ave Mujica to be added to Garupa just for them to announce they are not adding them to that game in favor of a more suitable game to fit their more serious mood. Like what? I get that maybe because MyGo and Ave Mujica have a lot of new fans, the older bands and content might be too overwhelming. body: The rhythm game aspect of the game (so far) has been fine and very fun. However, everyother aspect of the game is extremely unpolished and has many issues. There is still Japanese text littered throughout the game, the buttons in the character rank section do absolutely nothing and there are many features that will be released in future updates… why not release the game when it is actually finished? Another issue I’ve come across is most of the music shop songs are not in English, and the songs original singer / song difficulty levels cannot be viewed until AFTER the song is purchased. The currency to purchase covers is limited, and I should not have to guess this information before I claim the song. I’ve also had several instances where character models will not show and the voice lines don’t play. As a long time bang dream fan, this release is extremely disappointing and I hope the team addresses the issues quickly.

title: Great potential! A minor issue
body: I really love my experience with this game so far! For some credibility, I played a lot of Bandori during quarantine but quit in late 2023. In "Our Notes" I found the tutorial and user interface much more easier to navigate and everything seemed to be running smoothly! However, there is one issue of the gameplay that may seem minor at first, but kinda impact how I view the game as a whole. • Everything seems to be moving too fast. When getting into Gekiso lives, sometimes the loading and song selection move too quickly for your players to even process what happened. • When the wheel of songs is being spun it ends WAY too quickly before players can even take note of what other songs people wanted. I also think it's bad design to have them spin in a circle as they end up being upside down or sideways which makes it harder to tell. This also applies to sending stamps in live which mostly goes unused since there's no breathing room to interact with fellow players. ^ TLDR: I believe that the speed at which things move in Gekiso live should be slowed down so as to not make players feel rushed or promote fast-paced gameplay as it correlates with anxiety and feeling too antsy. ^ In no way am I implying that these issues are ruining the game, I just think it's important to catch these design choices early on so that they don't go unnoticed in future updates. I'm really enjoying this game so far and have found myself growing attached to the characters!

They actually cover some deep dark and realistic topics and emotions. It's everything I ever wanted for this genre that Miku and other games in this genre refused to give. If I have one complaint though, and unfortunately, it's a big complaint, after the initial starter push, premium currency is not easy to get. It's the same for a certain other game, but I quit that game long ago because of that. Just something to note.
